title: Lexical interop and role-marker coercion for model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: During recent model onboarding we observed intermittent chat rendering regressions where role markers (e.g., 'User:', 'Assistant:') were being tokenized differently than Redwood's canonical chat templates. This caused a mismatch between the published performance profile (token counts/latency estimates) and observed runtime behavior for a subset of models that use non-ASCII or multi-character delimiters.

Root cause hypothesis: Upstream model tokenizer variants sometimes split role markers into subtokens or treat delimiters as part of adjacent words. Our onboarding pipeline assumes canonical delimiter boundaries when producing sample prompts for profile generation. When delimiters are coerced differently at runtime, KV cache prefixing and batching heuristics produce different token distributions and occasionally lead to truncated structured output or inflated token counts.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, reversible preprocessing step during onboarding that: (1) infers delimiter/role-marker tokenization behavior for a given model, (2) generates a coercion shim that normalizes delimiters in the onboarding prompt set used for performance profile publication, and (3) emits metadata flags so the runtime can apply equivalent normalization when model pinning or fallback routing is used. This should preserve correctness for structured tool-calling and reduce profile/observed divergence.

Proposed solution:
1) Delimiter inference job: run a short probing harness that feeds a curated delimiter matrix (ASCII, unicode punctuation, multi-char markers) into the tokenizer and observes subtoken boundaries. Record canonicalization rules (prefix/suffix escapes, required whitespace).
2) Coercion shim generator: from the inference results produce a small set of deterministic rewrite rules that can be applied to onboarding prompt fixtures to normalize role markers into the model's tokenization-friendly form. Store the shim as plain text rules in the model metadata blob (e.g., 'delimiter_coercion_v1').
3) Profile rehydration: re-run the performance profile generation after applying the shim so the published token/latency estimates match real inference. Tag the published profile with 'coercion_applied' and the shim checksum.
4) Runtime hinting: expose the shim checksum as part of the model manifest so Redwood routing can opt-in to applying the same normalization at serving time for pinned models or when falling back to the onboarded variant.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full tokenizer patching vs shim: Patching tokenizer logic is high-risk and may break other workflows; a shim preserves the model tokenizer and keeps changes localized to onboarding and optional runtime normalization.
- Applying coercion globally at runtime may alter user prompts; therefore the runtime application should be opt-in and gated behind model pinning/fallback policies and documented in the manifest.

Testing & validation plan:
- Unit: delimiter inference unit tests covering the delimiter matrix and rule synthesis.
- Integration: synthetic fragment fuzz tests that apply shims to the onboarding corpus and compare token histograms before/after; ensure KV cache hit ratios and batching footprints align within 5% of expected profile.
- End-to-end: onboard a canary model with coercion and run a job that compares published profile to live telemetry for 24h.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (dev): land the inference harness and shim generator behind a feature flag. Create conftests and a GitHub PR for review.
- Phase 2 (canary): onboard 2 non-ASCII-delimiter models with the shim enabled; publish updated profiles. Observe telemetry vs profile and run automated acceptance.
- Phase 3 (opt-in runtime): expose runtime hint flag for Dedicated/Private customers for explicit opt-in. Document behavior in console and release notes.

Monitoring & success metrics:
- Primary success metric: reduction in profile/telemetry divergence measured as absolute token-count delta across sample prompts (target < 3% median).
- Secondary: reduction in structured-output truncation incidents (target 90% reduction for affected models).
- Operational: no more than one customer-facing regression related to prompt normalization during canary.

Artifacts & links: Confluence design doc (delimiter inference + shim format), onboarding harness repo, and initial PR (see attachments).

acceptance_criteria: Delimiter inference harness implemented and covered by unit tests.
Shim generator produces deterministic rules and is stored in model metadata with checksum.
Performance profile published after shim application and tagged with 'coercion_applied'.
Canary telemetry shows profile/observed token histogram median delta < 3% for canary models.
Runtime normalization is behind opt-in manifest flag; Console shows banner when enabled for a model.
Documentation and runbook updated for Support and Solutions engineering.
